# Michael Edward Bleich: professional due-diligence dossier

Research cut-off: November 4, 2026. Subject: Michael Edward Bleich, individual Central Registration Depository (CRD) number 4262671.

Prepared for the in-house diligence team from the reviewed official-record investigation. The manuscript brings the completed research together; it does not claim that every employment interval, corporate identity or proceeding has been established.

## Contents

1. Scope and principal findings
2. Identity and career chronology
3. Entities, funds and ownership
4. Investment-management events
5. Financial observations
6. Unresolved questions and next actions
7. Evidence, methods and review

Supporting appendices: [Claims and citations](claims.md), [document catalogue](documents.md), [people and entities](entities-and-roles.md), [events](events.md), [financial observations](financial-observations.md), and [conflicts and gaps](conflicts-and-gaps.md).

## 1. Scope and principal findings

### What the records establish

Official firm records identify Bleich by full name and CRD number in professional roles at Scout Trading, Ophir Partners and EntryPoint Capital. They establish particular role and ownership disclosures, rather than a complete employment history. The earlier Chase, Lehman and Barclays chronology and the alleged Inferent role remain unresolved. [[ID-C001]] [[ID-C003]] [[ID-C012]] [[SEC-C002]] [[EMP5-C07]] [[EMP5-C08]]

The main findings are:

| Finding | Evidence and limitation |
|---|---|
| The same professional identifier links Scout, Ophir and EntryPoint disclosures. | CRD 4262671 anchors the subject's identity. Filing and acquired-status dates must not be treated as complete employment intervals. [[ID-C001]] [[ID-C012]] [[SEC-C002]] [[EMP5-C03]] |
| Ownership records contain dated structures and unresolved legal identities. | MEB INC / MEB NY INC wording, ownership-band changes and candidate registry numbers require separate treatment. A September 2009 New York change entry does not establish a rename. [[EMP4-C09]] [[CORP5-C001]] [[CORP5-C003]] [[CORP5-C005]] |
| Adviser withdrawal records describe different circumstances. | Ophir reports advisory cessation in June 2017. Inferent says it would continue under an exemption in March 2020. EntryPoint's December 2021 withdrawal states a continued-registration eligibility reason and reports that business had not ceased. These are firm-filed administrative records. [[EP5-C004]] [[EP5-C005]] [[EP5-C006]] |
| The Scout Nasdaq settlement is a firm matter. | The $3 million fine is not a separate personal sanction against Bleich. The events chapter distinguishes settlement allegations, firm outcomes, arbitration and administrative filings. [[EVT-C001]] |
| Financial figures describe different measures. | EntryPoint reports $999,157,153 of regulatory assets under management (RAUM), measured September 30, 2026. The master's gross assets, ERA private-fund assets, offering sales and Form 13F holdings are separate measures. [[SEC-C007]] [[SEC-C008]] [[SEC-C010]] [[EP5-C011]] |
| Court and employment coverage remain incomplete. | Bounded searches do not establish an absence of proceedings or an absence of an unlisted employee role. No later court or payment record for the Scout/Wedbush award was established. [[LIT5-C04]] [[LIT5-C05]] [[EMP5-C07]] |

These findings support specific statements about the professional record. They do not support an overall clearance, a finding of personal misconduct from a firm settlement, or an estimate of Bleich's personal wealth or income.

### Scope and reading rules

The investigation covers historical professional roles, advisers, broker-dealers, funds, special-purpose vehicles, ownership intermediaries, regulatory matters and investment-management litigation. Personal civil proceedings and private home or family details are outside scope. Inferent and unresolved corporate candidates are included as conditional research branches, not established affiliations.

Official public records are the evidentiary basis. Third-party material is a lead only. A filing is attributed to its filer; hosting by a regulator does not make every assertion an independently adjudicated fact. The dossier labels official-record inferences and keeps the records that support them visible.

A missing result is described by its actual search scope. NYSCEF remains an accepted access gap. No PACER account was available. The five prior Library research files were inaccessible and have not been reconciled. Existing legacy repository material was excluded from research by instruction. The [follow-up instructions](../remaining-work-instructions.md) specify what remains needed.

Readers can follow each claim identifier to its supporting records and exact page or field locator. The evidence appendix retains the registered wording and classifications, including earlier formulations that later records qualify. Where an earlier access gap has been resolved, a current-reading note says so.

## 6. Unresolved questions and next actions

The remaining questions require particular records or better access. They cannot be resolved by rephrasing the current evidence. The [remaining-work instructions](../remaining-work-instructions.md) provide exact identifiers, permitted access routes and completion tests.

| Question | Record needed and completion test |
|---|---|
| What were the early employment periods? | Obtain a dated official individual history or an authenticated employment record in an official public filing. Match the subject, role and date precision. Registration and an RSU agreement do not establish every employment interval. |
| Did Bleich hold a role at Inferent? Was there an Ophir transaction? | Obtain a direct dated role disclosure or professional agreement, and a separate transaction instrument if a transfer is alleged. Overlapping associates and missing owner/executive entries do not settle either question. |
| What is the complete EntryPoint approval and legal-name history? | Obtain the application, receipt, approval and corporate-name instruments associated with CRD 313946 and SEC files 801-122062, 802-125863 and 801-130798. The dual 2024 flags already have a supported procedural explanation; approval and compliance are distinct. |
| Which registry entities are the disclosed owners? | Obtain original instruments with an identifier bridge for MEB, Finch, NAYS, the EntryPoint intermediaries and EP Fund GP. Preserve the historical United ownership chain without joining similarly named banks. |
| What caused the ownership and date differences? | Obtain ownership or transaction instruments for the Scout and Ophir changes. Preserve June/August 2012 and March/June 2016 observations until their specific meanings can be reconciled. |
| Were there later proceedings or payment on the Scout award? | Obtain a target-linked confirmation, vacatur, appeal or satisfaction record. Keep the award amount, possible interest and actual collection separate. |
| What remains missing from the fund and adviser originals? | Obtain Ophir brochure 247246, EntryPoint brochure 1061309, the March 2019 Inferent Part 2A original and the relevant Cayman formation/registered-statement or GP-change instruments. |
| Can the financial discrepancies be resolved? | Obtain an original correction or supporting record for the EntryPoint 2024 Q3 13F and Inferent withdrawal balance sheet. Establish measurement dates; retain the original figures. |
| Can the prior research be reconciled? | Obtain access to the five referenced Library files. Build a claim-by-claim crosswalk to the retained official originals instead of importing their conclusions. |

This action table summarizes the separate instructions; it does not add factual conclusions. The [conflict appendix](conflicts-and-gaps.md) retains all 26 registered issues, including the award's requested-relief figures, Cboe terminology and dates, Scout membership/report-period differences, historical fund names, financial discrepancies and rejected identity joins. Some entries describe historical uncertainty now partly resolved. Current-reading notes preserve that distinction.

### Access boundaries

NYSCEF is deliberately left as an access gap under the user's instruction. The separate New York Law Reporting Bureau search also encountered an access challenge and produced no native name-search result. Those are different limitations. [[LIT5-C02]]

The searches across published opinions, federal and state sources and the CFTC content index are bounded. They do not cover all court dockets or all agency records. Additional public or authorized records may change the findings. No new responsive proceeding was established by the latest searches. [[LIT5-C01]] [[LIT5-C03]] [[LIT5-C04]]

## 7. Evidence, methods and review

### Evidence package

The reviewed register contains 247 assertions linked through 444 evidence references to 396 retained source representations. The entity register has 37 entity entries and eight people; it includes candidates and conditional relationships. Its 67 financial observations and nine event entries are records with stated scopes, not independent estimates of wealth or a count of personal sanctions.

The dossier reproduces every indexed assertion and every evidence link in the [claim appendix](claims.md). It also supplies complete entity, role, relationship, event, financial and conflict appendices. The main narrative selects and explains the substantive findings. Search logs, failed responses and repetitive disclosure observations remain available in the supporting registers rather than interrupting the account.

| Review need | Where to look |
|---|---|
| Verify a sentence | Follow its claim link to the exact source locator and retained file. |
| Inspect source authority and preservation | Use the document catalogue for source class, original URL, retrieval time, filing period, accession and SHA256. |
| Check names and historical relationships | Use the people/entities appendix and its relationship notes. |
| Trace a numerical observation | Use the financial appendix for metric, units, filing date, measurement date and qualification. |
| Distinguish sanctions from other events | Use the event register and linked claims; administrative withdrawals have no disciplinary respondent. |
| Understand an unresolved issue | Read the conflict appendix and the separate follow-up instructions. |
| Reproduce coverage | Use the unchanged [JSON index](../evidence-index.json), [SQLite index](../evidence-index.sqlite), [CSV tables](../tables/), [search log](../tables/search_logs.csv), and [retrieval attempts](../tables/retrieval_attempts.csv). |

### Preservation and interpretation

The records retain original source bytes, URLs, retrieval times in UTC, filing or docket identifiers, page/field locators and SHA256 hashes. Official PDFs, regulator-hosted archive members and extracted text have distinct source classes. A failed response is an access record, not evidence about the underlying case or person.

Some large SEC tables are retained as exact compressed archive members with size, checksum and reconstruction metadata. Target extracts are derivatives. The same FilingID can appear in both registered-adviser and exempt-reporting-adviser exports; that does not create two applications or two events. [[EP5-C001]] [[EP5-C003]] [[EMP5-C02]]

PDF locators refer to physical pages starting at one. CSV ordinal conventions are stated in the relevant packet: employment scans use data rows excluding the header, while the withdrawal packet uses header-inclusive ordinals. Source filing and signature timestamps are not converted into UTC when their original timezone is unknown. Retrieval timestamps are recorded separately.

The manuscript follows the [editorial standard](../presentation/dossier-editorial-standard.md). Plain English and Humanizer guide readability. Quotations, necessary legal terminology, identity uncertainty and date precision take precedence over stylistic shortening. The source register and originals are unchanged by dossier writing.

### Review record and version

The underlying research has separate source and normalized-index QA, linked from [independent research QA](../independent-qa.md). Dossier review records appear in [the review folder](review/). The dossier's [coverage record](coverage.json) identifies every narrative citation and every appendix entry. Its [release record](release.json) identifies the input research commit and checks performed for this manuscript.

This dossier is a complete written account of the assembled research as of its stated cut-off. The full-career investigation remains open on the specific questions listed above.
